record.paper_title: Ten Conferences WORDS: Open Problems and Conjectures
record.original_question: If p is k-avoidable that a k-letter circular word of length |p| avoiding p exist.

evidence.quote: If p is k-avoidable that a k-letter circular word of length |p| avoiding p exist.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a finite alphabet and let E be an alphabet of variables, disjoint from A. A pattern is a nonempty word p ∈ E*. An occurrence of the pattern p in a word w ∈ A* is a nonerasing morphism h : E* → A* such that h(p) is a factor of w. A word w avoids p if there is no occurrence of p in w. A pattern p is said to be k-avoidable if there exists an infinite word over a k-letter alphabet that avoids p. A circular word of length n over an alphabet A is an equivalence class of words a_0 a_1 … a_{n−1} ∈ A^n under cyclic rotation; a pattern p is said to occur in such a circular word if it occurs (in the above sense) as a factor of some (equivalently every) linearization a_i a_{i+1} … a_{i+n−1} a_i a_{i+1} … (read with indices modulo n) of length at least |h(p)|.

Prove or disprove: for every pattern p and every integer k ≥ 1, if p is k-avoidable, then there exists a circular word over a k-letter alphabet of length |p| (the length of the pattern p, i.e. the number of variable occurrences in p) that avoids p.
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted search did not turn up a published resolution of this specific conjecture relating k-avoidability of a pattern p to the existence of a k-ary circular word of length |p| avoiding p. Related work concerns repetition thresholds for circular words and Cassaigne-type avoidability bounds, but none of the located sources state the conjecture as solved.

status_evidence.title: Repetition Threshold for Circular Words
status_evidence.snippet: For any n there exists a k-ary circular word of length n containing no repetition of exponent greater than CRT(k).
status_evidence.claim: Circular-word avoidance results exist in the literature, but address repetition thresholds rather than the stated pattern-avoidance/circular-word conjecture.

status_evidence.title: Avoiding or Limiting Regularities in Words
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on pattern avoidance, k-avoidability, and Cassaigne's conjectures.
status_evidence.claim: Standard surveys of avoidability do not record this circular-word conjecture as resolved.
